answer: Cost-priced identity resists sybils: before transacting, an agent must lock a refundable bond and finish a resource-heavy verifiable computation. Each fake account carries real capital and compute cost, so a farm pays per identity. Agents publish signed attestations, a quill recording who vouched for whom, so faults are traceable. When a comet of new identities appears overnight, sparse self-referential vouching exposes the cluster and bonded stakes get slashed; a lone sparrow of doubt against one account propagates along those edges. Attackers face linear cost for diminishing influence.
